blocks.s: Bernard sets forth the famous scala claustralium — the ladder of those in the cloister — by which the soul ascends to God: lectio (reading), meditatio (meditation), oratio (prayer), and contemplatio (contemplation). By diligent reading the mind receives the material of divine truth; by meditation it chews and digests what has been received; by prayer it lifts the purified and enkindled heart to God; and by contemplation it is raised above itself into the light of the divine presence. This ladder is not always ascended step by step in visible succession, for the grace of contemplation is freely given; but it describes the ordinary preparation and proximate disposition of the contemplative soul.
